traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), orders 50 Loganiales, 51 Apocynales and 52 Rubiales and the gentian family, which APG joins as Gentianales: leaves opposite (whorled in some madders, rarely alternate in the dogbanes), simple or rarely compound; petals united; stamens as many as the corolla lobes, on the corolla.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb, Gentianales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): leaves opposite, joined by a line across the node. DELTA: Rubiaceae and Gentianaceae usually opposite and decussate.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: APweb, Gentianales page (read 2026-10-16): flowers usually radially symmetric with fused petals. DELTA: Rubiaceae, Apocynaceae, Gentianaceae regular.

traits.corolla_shape.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Rubiaceae corolla tubular or salver-shaped (the largest family, two thirds of candidates); Apocynaceae funnel- or salver-shaped; Gentianaceae bell, funnel, rotate or salver. Weighting by Rubiaceae.

traits.sexual_system.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Apocynaceae and Asclepiadaceae hermaphrodite; Rubiaceae and Gentianaceae usually so (Rubiaceae with some monoecious, dioecious, polygamous).

traits.life_span.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Rubiaceae mostly trees and shrubs; Apocynaceae mostly lianas and shrubs; Asclepiadaceae perennial; Gentianaceae mostly herbs, with annuals and biennials. 'Usually perennial' by species weight.

traits.hypanthium.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): no free hypanthium described for Rubiaceae, Apocynaceae or Gentianaceae; the ones with candidates that state it say false.

traits.rosette.note: DELTA Gentianaceae (read 2026-10-16): some species with a basal rosette; Rubiaceae and Apocynaceae woody or climbing. Inferred.
